metadata.title: Pembrolizumab with cisplatin and definitive cervical chemoradiotherapy
metadata.indication: Adults with FIGO 2014 stage III–IVA locally advanced cervical cancer who have received no prior definitive treatment. External beam radiotherapy is followed by brachytherapy.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

contexts.duration_text: Up to 20 cycles over a maximum of 24 months, stopping earlier for progression or unacceptable toxicity.
contexts.source_schedule_interval_label: Cycles 1–5 every 21 days, then cycles 6–20 every 42 days

encoding_maturity.label: Source-mapped feasibility build; independent clinical and pharmacy review pending

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Initiate under a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Discuss each modification with a consultant. Pembrolizumab dose reduction is not recommended; treat immune toxicity by withholding or permanent discontinuation as indicated.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Independent clinical and oncology pharmacy validation is pending.

indications.description: Adults with FIGO 2014 stage III–IVA locally advanced cervical cancer who have received no prior definitive treatment. External beam radiotherapy is followed by brachytherapy.

treatment.schedule_summary: Cisplatin 40 mg/m² is given with radiation in cycles 1 and 2. Pembrolizumab starts at 200 mg every 21 days and changes to 400 mg every 42 days at cycle 6. Cycles 1–5 are 21 days. Cycles 6–20 are 42 days. Treat for up to 24 months, stopping earlier for disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
treatment.duration_text: Cycles 1–5 are 21 days. Cycles 6–20 are 42 days. Treat for up to 24 months, stopping earlier for disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

administration.note: Prehydration and posthydration per local policy. Give before same-day radiation.

treatment_phases.duration_text: Administer pembrolizumab first, then cisplatin; radiotherapy follows the cisplatin infusion.
notes: Administer pembrolizumab first, then cisplatin; radiotherapy follows the cisplatin infusion.

treatment_phases.duration_text: One cisplatin dose on each listed treatment day. The required day-15 dose applies only to cycle 1.

pembro_immune_nephritis_assessed.label: Renal abnormality clinically assessed as immune-mediated nephritis?
pembro_immune_nephritis_assessed.help: Yes means the treating clinician has assessed immune-mediated toxicity and evaluated alternative causes; a raised laboratory result alone does not establish this. No or blank keeps an abnormal result in a clinical-review pathway. This does not require biopsy confirmation. EMA Keytruda IV SmPC §4.4; NCCP Table 5 applies to immune-related adverse reactions.

creatinine_ratio_baseline_or_uln.label: Creatinine (× ULN; immune-nephritis threshold assessment)
creatinine_ratio_baseline_or_uln.help: ULN only, never fold-change from baseline. A raised result requires clinical assessment of immune causality and alternative causes before source hold/stop rules are applied. Stable chronic impairment remains a separate no-adjustment pathway.

pembro_immune_hepatitis_assessed.label: Liver abnormality clinically assessed as immune-mediated hepatitis?
pembro_immune_hepatitis_assessed.help: Yes means the treating clinician has assessed immune-mediated toxicity and evaluated alternative causes; a raised laboratory result alone does not establish this. No or blank keeps an abnormal result in a clinical-review pathway. This does not require biopsy confirmation. EMA Keytruda IV SmPC §4.4; NCCP Table 5 applies to immune-related adverse reactions.

alt_ast_uln_multiple.label: AST or ALT (× ULN)
alt_ast_uln_multiple.help: Highest AST or ALT multiple of its ULN in immune-hepatitis assessment; investigate other causes. A laboratory elevation alone does not diagnose immune hepatitis; record clinical attribution separately.

pembro_restart_requested.label: Assess restarting pembrolizumab after an immune-related treatment hold

pembro_source_recovery_complete.label: Source-specific recovery criteria met for the prior immune event
pembro_source_recovery_complete.help: Usually grade 0–1. Use the Table 5 endocrine exception when applicable: prior grade 3–4 endocrinopathy improved to grade 2 or lower and controlled with hormone replacement. This is not a global treatment clearance.

pembro_steroid_management_complete.label: Required corticosteroid management/taper completed or not needed
pembro_steroid_management_complete.help: Confirm against the specific toxicity and Table 5 endocrine exception. The existing 12-week failure/taper stop rules remain applicable; do not infer a new universal restart dose threshold.

pembro_consultant_restart_approved.label: Consultant has confirmed the post-toxicity restart plan

pembro_prior_permanent_stop.label: Any previous event meeting pembrolizumab permanent-discontinuation criteria
pembro_prior_permanent_stop.help: Review the documented immune-event history even when current symptoms and laboratory values have recovered. A prior permanent-stop event is not cleared by recovery or steroid taper.

eligibility: Adults with FIGO 2014 stage III–IVA locally advanced cervical cancer who have received no prior definitive treatment. External beam radiotherapy is followed by brachytherapy.
ECOG 0–1; an individual consultant may consider ECOG 2. Adequate hepatic, renal and marrow function.
exclusions: Hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab, cisplatin or an excipient, pre-existing renal impairment, significant hearing impairment or tinnitus, pregnancy and breastfeeding.
Consult the NCCP previous PD-1/PD-L1 treatment guidance.

baseline: FBC, renal/liver profile, blood glucose and thyroid function. Consider audiology according to clinical findings.
regular: FBC, renal/liver profile and glucose before each cycle. Thyroid function every 3–6 weeks. Cortisol and audiology when clinically indicated.
Monitor treatment response and toxicity with the supervising consultant.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: 00943 p7 assigns high emetogenic risk to cisplatin and minimal risk to pembrolizumab alone. Active drugs determine each visit.

supportive_care.pre_medications: No routine drug-specific premedication. Use the local cisplatin high-risk antiemetic protocol with cisplatin and verify hydration and electrolytes.
supportive_care.hydration: Pre- and posthydration on every cisplatin day. Check magnesium and potassium and the local hydration plan. Monitor for fluid overload.
